name: Amman & Petra
tagline: Hills of Roman ruins above the road to Petra.
bestMonths: Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Sep and Oct
whenBlurb: March to May and October to November bring wildflower deserts, mild Petra walks and Petra by Night's candlelit Treasury; summer bakes the canyons and Amman turns cold in deep winter.

ourTake.lede: Treat Amman as the base and Petra as the reason. Give the capital a day for the Citadel and the Roman theatre, then drive the King's Highway south rather than the fast desert road, the wadis and Crusader castles are the point. At Petra, arrive at opening and walk past the Treasury to the Monastery; most people never get that far.
ourTake.comeIf: You want Petra, Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea threaded into one unhurried, deeply historic journey.
ourTake.skipIf: You want beaches, shopping or a resort week; this is a trip for the curious traveller.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel Amman
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025)
items.description: A palatial tower on the highest of the White City's seven hills, Four Seasons polish, the surest hands in Jordan.

items.name: The St. Regis Amman
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide (2025)
items.description: Butler service on every floor and Levantine art throughout, the St. Regis ritual, brought to the diplomatic quarter.

items.name: Fairmont Amman
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide (2025)
items.description: A glass tower over the new downtown, floor-to-ceiling city views, Le Labo baths, beside the Four Seasons and St. Regis.

items.name: Kempinski Hotel Ishtar Dead Sea
credentials: Travel + Leisure World's Best, among the world's top 500 hotels, best in Jordan
Condé Nast Traveler, Top 5 Middle East resorts
World Luxury Spa Awards / World Travel Awards, Jordan's Best Hotel Spa (2017–2019)
items.description: Nine pools and hanging gardens down to the shore, a Babylon-inspired resort on the longest private beach in Jordan.

items.name: Grand Hyatt Amman
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards 2023, Top 20 Hotels in the Middle East
items.description: A long-standing grand house near Rainbow Street, an in-house art gallery and four restaurants, quietly reliable.

items.name: W Amman
credentials: Marriott Luxury Portfolio, W Hotels flagship, Jordan
items.description: A bold contemporary statement in the new downtown, a canyon-walk entrance inspired by Petra, and W's design energy.

items.name: Mövenpick Resort & Residence Dead Sea
credentials: World Travel Awards, Jordan's Leading Resort (multiple years)
items.description: An Arabic village of low stone buildings and gardens sloping to the sea, the award-winning Zara Spa its centrepiece.

items.name: Mövenpick Resort Petra
credentials: Accor / Mövenpick 5-star, unrivalled position at the Petra entrance
items.description: Fifty metres from the Petra gate, Levantine mosaics and marble, and the shortest walk to the Rose City there is.

items.name: Evason Ma'In Hot Springs
credentials: Six Senses group heritage, spa set beneath a natural hot-spring waterfall
items.description: A canyon oasis 264 m below sea level, a hot-spring waterfall cascading into the pool, the setting is the star.

items.name: Memories Aicha Luxury Camp
credentials: Within the UNESCO World Heritage Wadi Rum Protected Area (2011)
items.description: Glass-domed 'Martian' bubble suites open to the stars, deep in the Valley of the Moon, the desert night, in comfort.

items.name: The Siq, Petra
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
New7Wonders of the World, Petra
items.description: The 1.2km sandstone gorge that opens Petra: walls soaring 80 metres, narrowing to a slit, until the Treasury flashes into view at the end. Walk it slowly at first light with a private guide before the coaches arrive, and let the children run the last stretch to the reveal.

items.name: The Treasury (Al-Khazneh), Petra
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
New7Wonders of the World, Petra
items.description: The single most recognisable facade on earth, 40 metres of rose-red rock carved straight into the cliff by the Nabataeans. Arrive at dawn for the light on the columns and space for a proper family photograph, then take mint tea at a cliffside spot facing it.

items.name: The Monastery (Ad-Deir), Petra
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
New7Wonders of the World, Petra
items.description: Petra's largest monument, wider and taller than the Treasury, reached by roughly 800 rock-cut steps high into the mountains. Well worth a second day; older travellers can ride a donkey up while the fit hike, and the view from the ridge opposite is the reward.

items.name: The Royal Tombs, Petra
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
items.description: A row of grand mausoleums carved into the cliff below the theatre, the Urn, Silk, Corinthian and Palace tombs, their stone banded in swirls of colour. Climb at late afternoon when the west light sets the whole facade glowing.

items.name: The High Place of Sacrifice, Petra
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
items.description: A Nabataean altar platform on a summit reached by a stepped trail, with a sweeping view over the entire valley of tombs. A rewarding morning climb for active families; a guide brings the ritual carvings to life.

items.name: The Street of Facades & Colonnaded Street, Petra
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
items.description: Beyond the Treasury the canyon widens into a whole carved city, rows of tomb facades, a Roman theatre cut from rock, and a colonnaded main street. This is where a full day inside Petra earns its keep, ideally at an unhurried pace with a driver waiting at the gate.

items.name: Petra by Night
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Petra
items.description: Three or four evenings a week the Siq is lit by some 1,500 candles and you walk in near-silence to the Treasury for music and story under the stars. A quietly magical close to a Petra day; book ahead and go on a night your camp or hotel can arrange transfers.

items.name: Little Petra (Siq al-Barid)
items.description: A miniature Nabataean canyon a short drive north of Petra, far quieter, with a rare painted ceiling in one of its rock-cut halls. A gentle, crowd-free hour that pairs beautifully with a long lunch at one of the boutique lodges nearby.

items.name: The Amman Citadel (Jabal al-Qala'a)
items.description: On the city's highest hill, layered with Roman, Byzantine and Umayyad remains and a grandstand view over the white houses of Amman. The obvious first stop; a private guide turns the scattered stones into a clear story for three generations at once.

items.name: Temple of Hercules, Amman Citadel
items.description: Two towering Roman columns and a giant carved stone hand are all that remain of a 2nd-century temple that would have outsized anything in Rome. Golden hour here, with the city falling away below, is one of Amman's finest photographs.

items.name: The Umayyad Palace, Amman Citadel
items.description: An 8th-century audience hall crowned by a reconstructed dome, the most photogenic corner of the Citadel and cool inside on a hot afternoon. The domed chamber and vast underground cistern reward a slow look with someone who can explain them.

items.name: The Roman Theatre, Amman
items.description: A 6,000-seat theatre cut into the hillside in the 2nd century, still steeply dramatic in the heart of downtown. Climb to the top row for the view; the two small folklore museums flanking it are a quick, worthwhile add.

items.name: The Jordan Museum
items.description: Jordan's flagship museum in Ras al-Ayn, home to the 9,000-year-old Ain Ghazal statues, among the oldest large human figures ever made, and copper-scroll material from the Dead Sea Scrolls. Air-conditioned, beautifully laid out and ideal for a hot midday with children.

items.name: King Abdullah I Mosque
items.description: Amman's landmark mosque, its vast blue mosaic dome visible across the city, built 1982–89 and open to respectful non-Muslim visitors outside prayer times. A serene, cool interior; robes are provided and a discreet guide smooths the visit for a family.

items.name: Rainbow Street & Downtown Souks, Amman
items.description: The city's most walkable stretch, cafes, galleries and rooftop views on Rainbow Street, spice, gold and textile souks tumbling downhill into Al-Balad. Best explored on foot late afternoon; a good private guide knows which lanes are worth the detour.

items.name: The Royal Automobile Museum, Amman
items.description: Some 70-plus cars and motorcycles from the late King Hussein's collection, from a 1916 Cadillac of the Arab Revolt to a Mercedes gullwing, a Ferrari F40 and the Aston Martin. A genuine crowd-pleaser for car-loving teenagers and grandfathers alike, set in King Hussein Park.

items.name: Darat al Funun, Amman
items.description: A hillside compound of restored 1920s houses and a small Byzantine ruin, now Amman's leading home for Arab contemporary art, with gardens, a library and a quiet cafe overlooking the old city. A calm, cultured hour away from the heat and crowds.

items.name: The Jara Souk & Wild Jordan Center, Amman
items.description: The Friday Souk Jara for local craft and the RSCN's Wild Jordan cafe for one of the city's best terrace views and honest Jordanian cooking. Both are easy, characterful stops; Wild Jordan is reliably good for vegetarian and Jain-aware family dining.

items.name: Hashem & Habibah, Downtown Amman
items.description: Two Amman institutions minutes apart: Hashem for 24-hour falafel, hummus and fatteh in a downtown alley, and Habibah since 1951 for the definitive plate of warm kunafa. The most authentic bite in the city, and both are naturally vegetarian-friendly.

items.name: 4x4 Desert Safari, Wadi Rum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wadi Rum Protected Area
items.description: A private jeep tour across the red sand of the Valley of the Moon, towering rock walls, dunes, springs and canyons that doubled as Mars on film. The essential Wadi Rum half-day; camel or horse can be added for the children.

items.name: A Night in a Luxury Bedouin Camp, Wadi Rum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wadi Rum Protected Area
items.description: Sleep in a domed or Martian-style suite with a private terrace, a zarb dinner cooked underground, and a sky thick with stars. The finest camps offer proper beds, ensuite bathrooms and discreet service, an unforgettable, safe night out for multi-generation families.

items.name: Um Fruth & Burdah Rock Bridges, Wadi Rum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wadi Rum Protected Area
items.description: Two natural stone arches, the low, climbable Um Fruth and the lofty Burdah, one of the highest rock bridges anywhere. Um Fruth is an easy scramble for a family photo; Burdah is a guided half-day for the surefooted.

items.name: Khazali Canyon & Lawrence's Spring, Wadi Rum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wadi Rum Protected Area
items.description: A cool, shaded slot canyon walled with ancient Thamudic petroglyphs, and the greenery of a spring tied to T.E. Lawrence. Gentle, atmospheric stops on a jeep route, the carvings fascinate children when a Bedouin guide reads them.

items.name: Hot-Air Ballooning over Wadi Rum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wadi Rum Protected Area
items.description: A sunrise flight above the desert, drifting over red dunes and sandstone islands as the light turns them gold. The most serene view of Rum there is, a private basket can be arranged for a special morning.

items.name: Stargazing in Wadi Rum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wadi Rum Protected Area
items.description: With almost no light pollution, Rum is among the world's great skies; camps run telescope sessions on the Milky Way and planets, best around the new moon. A quiet, wondrous close to a desert day for all ages.

items.name: Floating in the Dead Sea
items.description: Bob effortlessly on the surface of the lowest point on earth, 430-odd metres below sea level, water so salt-dense you cannot sink. A must-do novelty for the whole family; go from a resort beach with fresh-water showers close by.

items.name: Dead Sea Mud & Spa
items.description: Coat yourself in mineral-black mud, let it dry, rinse it off in the sea, then retreat to a world-class spa, the Kempinski Ishtar's is among the largest in the Middle East. A restorative day of pampering for multi-generation travellers.

items.name: Jerash Roman Ruins
items.description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities anywhere, the colonnaded Oval Plaza, an 800-metre chariot-rutted Cardo, the Temple of Artemis, Hadrian's Arch and a hippodrome. A day trip from Amman that astonishes; a guide and an early start make it.

items.name: The Madaba Mosaic Map
items.description: In a working Greek Orthodox church, the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land, a 6th-century floor mosaic of some two million tiles. Small but extraordinary; Madaba's mosaic workshops and stone-set churches fill a rewarding half-day.

items.name: Mount Nebo
items.description: The height from which Moses is said to have seen the Promised Land, with a fine memorial church, ancient mosaics and a view stretching to the Dead Sea and, on a clear day, Jerusalem. A moving, easy stop near Madaba for any family.

items.name: Bethany Beyond the Jordan (The Baptism Site)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Baptism Site (Bethany Beyond the Jordan)
items.description: The believed site of Christ's baptism on the east bank of the Jordan, excavated churches, pools and the riverbank itself. A serene, deeply meaningful visit; access is by official shuttle with a guide, so plan through your concierge.

items.name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
items.description: Jordan's largest reserve, tumbling from cool mountains to desert lowlands across four ecological zones, with over 800 plant species and rare Nubian ibex. Hike the Wadi Dana trail or simply take the sunset view; a wild, restorative counterpoint to the ruins.

items.name: Feynan Ecolodge, Dana
items.description: A candlelit, solar-run lodge at the desert end of Dana, named among the world's top eco-lodges by National Geographic, reached the last stretch by Bedouin 4x4. Star-bathed nights, Bedouin hospitality and slow days, a rare, soulful stay for the curious.

items.name: Diving & Snorkelling in Aqaba
items.description: The Red Sea at Aqaba holds warm, clear water year-round, healthy coral and famous sites like the sunken tank and the Cedar Pride wreck within a protected marine park. Gentle house reefs suit first-time snorkellers and children; private boat dives suit the certified.

items.name: Aqaba Marine Park & Beach Resorts
items.description: Jordan's warm-water resort town on the Gulf of Aqaba, the natural place to unwind after Petra and Wadi Rum with beach clubs, glass-bottom boats and easy family swimming. A relaxed coda to a Jordan itinerary, with views across to three countries.

items.name: Qasr Amra (Qusayr 'Amra)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Quseir Amra
items.description: A small 8th-century Umayyad bath-house whose walls and dome carry the finest surviving early-Islamic frescoes, hunts, musicians and a rare painted zodiac. There is nothing else quite like it in the world; the highlight of the desert-castle loop east of Amman.

items.name: Qasr Kharana
items.description: A square, near-perfect Umayyad building in the open desert, long thought a fort but likely a caravan inn, its rooms ranged around a courtyard. A striking, atmospheric stop on the eastern loop, quick to see and photogenic against empty land.

items.name: Qasr Azraq
items.description: A black-basalt fortress rebuilt in the 13th century and famous as T.E. Lawrence's winter headquarters during the Arab Revolt. History buffs and Lawrence readers relish it; pair with the nearby Azraq wetland reserve.

items.name: Umm Qais (Gadara)
items.description: A Decapolis city on a green plateau in Jordan's far north, its black-and-white theatre and colonnaded street looking out over the Sea of Galilee and the Golan. Panoramic, uncrowded and lovely at sunset, with a well-regarded local restaurant on site.

items.name: Ajloun Castle (Qal'at ar-Rabad)
items.description: A 12th-century Ayyubid fortress raised under Saladin to face the Crusaders, commanding wooded hills and long views over the Jordan Valley. A satisfying stop for children who like castles, often paired with Jerash and Umm Qais on a northern day.

items.name: As-Salt (The Place of Tolerance)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, As-Salt, the Place of Tolerance and Urban Hospitality
items.description: A honey-limestone Ottoman-era town on three hills, famed for its yellow-stone mansions and a lived tradition of Muslim-Christian harmony. A gentle, authentic half-day of stepped lanes and guest-house hospitality, a short drive from Amman.

items.name: Umm ar-Rasas
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Um er-Rasas (Kastrom Mefa'a)
items.description: A quiet archaeological site south of Madaba whose Church of St Stephen holds one of the Byzantine world's great mosaic floors, mapping the cities of the region, alongside a rare 15-metre stylite tower. An off-the-track gem for those who loved the Madaba map.

items.name: The King's Highway Drive
items.description: The ancient road threading Madaba, Wadi Mujib's canyon overlooks, Karak's Crusader castle and Dana on the scenic way south to Petra. With a private driver it turns the transfer into the journey, the slow, storied route rather than the fast desert highway.

items.name: Karak Castle
items.description: A hulking Crusader fortress on a spur above the King's Highway, with vaulted halls and dungeons to explore and enormous valley views. A dramatic break on the drive to Petra that children and history-lovers both enjoy.

items.name: Wadi Mujib Siq Trail
items.description: Jordan's 'Grand Canyon' meeting the Dead Sea, a wet gorge trail where you wade and scramble up a river between soaring walls, run by the RSCN in season. An exhilarating adventure for fit teenagers and adults, minutes from the Dead Sea resorts.

items.name: Ma'in Hot Springs
items.description: Thermal waterfalls tumbling steaming into pools in a desert gorge below sea level, with a spa resort built around them. A relaxing, slightly wild interlude near the Dead Sea, easy for all generations to enjoy.

items.name: Fakhreldin
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 11
items.description: Lebanese fine dining in a former prime minister's villa, immaculate mezze and service, the grand Amman institution since 1997.

items.name: Alee
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 13
items.description: Chef Ali Ghzawi's modern Levantine cooking, home flavours retold through storytelling and playful texture.

items.name: Dara Dining by Sara Aqel
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 18, Highest New Entry Award
items.description: Season-led cooking with an Italian thread, in a beautifully restored villa, the most talked-about opening in the city.

items.name: Shams El Balad
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 8, Best Restaurant in Jordan
items.description: Farm-to-table Jordanian home cooking in a sunlit old house, the freshest, most honest table in the city.

items.name: Sufra
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 20
items.description: Traditional Jordanian cooking in a converted 1950s villa with a garden terrace, the classic Amman lunch.

items.name: Beit Sitti
credentials: 50 Best Discovery (World's 50 Best), Amman
items.description: 'Grandmother's house', a hands-on home-cooking experience in a restored family home, cooking then sharing the meal.

items.name: Hashem
credentials: Documented Amman institution, a national landmark of Jordanian cuisine
items.description: The city's iconic falafel-and-hummus house since the 1950s, open all hours, once served the royal family, still unbeatable.

items.name: Sekrab
credentials: 50 Best Discovery (World's 50 Best), Amman
items.description: A rooftop of found-object 'junk' art and open-air seating, quirky Jordanian plates over the old city's lights.

items.name: 13C, Bar in the Back
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 36 (the only Jordanian venue on the list run as a bar)
items.description: A hidden speakeasy behind an unmarked door, the most serious, most awarded mixology in Jordan.

items.name: Cantaloupe Gastropub
credentials: Widely cited as Amman's landmark Rainbow Street rooftop bar
items.description: The original Rainbow Street rooftop, iconic three-hill views over downtown and a long, easy Amman evening.

items.name: District Urban Rooftop
credentials: Widely cited among Amman's premier cocktail rooftops
items.description: A chic high-rise rooftop in the new downtown, inventive cocktails and a sweeping skyline panorama.

items.name: Sekrab Rooftop
credentials: 50 Best Discovery (World's 50 Best), Amman
items.description: Open-air, junk-art rooftop that turns from supper to a lively late crowd over the lights of the old city.

plan.heading: 5 days in Amman & Petra, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Citadel above Amman with the Temple of Hercules, then the Roman theatre below.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch of mezze at Sufra in a restored villa, then the galleries of Jabal Al Weibdeh.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner and a nightcap at the Four Seasons Amman overlooking the hills.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive to Jerash, one of the best-preserved Roman cities, walking its oval forum and colonnaded street early.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch in the Ajloun hills, then the crusader castle of Qal'at ar-Rabad.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Return to Amman for dinner at Fakhreldin, the city's finest Levantine table.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: The desert and the descent south

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive to the Dead Sea, floating in the mineral water and lunch at the shore.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Continue south along the King's Highway, pausing at the Wadi Mujib overlook.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Check into the Petra Marriott or a fine local riad, an early dinner before Petra.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Enter the Siq at first light to reach the Treasury before the crowds, then the Street of Facades.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Climb the 800 steps to the Monastery for lunch and the view, then the Royal Tombs in soft light.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Petra by Candlelight through the lit Siq, then dinner back at the hotel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive into Wadi Rum, a private 4x4 through the red sands and rock bridges of T.E. Lawrence's desert.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch under an overhang, then the Nabataean inscriptions and Khazali canyon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sunset from a dune and dinner at a Bedouin luxury camp beneath the Milky Way.

items.name: Jabal Amman / Rainbow Street
items.description: For the walkable, café-lined old heart of the capital, near the galleries and downtown souks.

items.name: Abdoun
items.description: For the modern, embassy-district polish, the smarter hotels and restaurants, quieter and greener.

items.name: Wadi Musa
items.description: The town at Petra's gate; base here so you can be first through the Siq at opening.

events.name: Jerash Festival
events.note: Jordan's flagship culture festival, staged among the floodlit Roman ruins north of Amman.

events.name: Petra Desert Marathon
events.note: A trail race through the ancient city and surrounding desert, drawing runners from around the world.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Amman's Abdoun and the Four Seasons area suit a city base; for Petra, stay close to the gate and enter at opening to have the Treasury near-empty. Dress modestly away from hotels, bring proper walking shoes and sun cover, and consider Petra by Night on its scheduled evenings.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive at Queen Alia International (AMM) south of Amman, where a fast-track greeter and private car begin the transfer, about forty minutes to the capital, and roughly three hours south to Petra along the Desert Highway.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver with a good vehicle is the way to cover Jordan's distances; Petra itself is walked, and the fit should keep an early start for the Monastery climb, with horses and carts available for the Siq.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: An eSIM from Zain or Orange Jordan gives dependable 4G in Amman and around Petra; coverage is patchier in the desert, so plan for gaps in Wadi Rum.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The Jordanian dinar (JOD) is strong and cash-friendly; cards work in Amman hotels and better restaurants, but carry dinars for Petra, guides and tips, where 10 percent is the norm.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Spring (March-May) and autumn (September-November) are ideal: mild 20-25C days for Petra and Wadi Rum. Avoid December-February, when Petra turns cold and wet with desert nights below freezing, and peak summer, when it tops 38C.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi to Amman on Air India, roughly 5.5 hours, or via the Gulf hubs on Emirates, Qatar Airways or Royal Jordanian in business. Routing through Doha or Dubai lets you use a first-class lounge and often improves the cabin over the direct service. Petra is about a three-hour private transfer south of Amman.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Recommended: hepatitis A and typhoid, with routine vaccinations current. Jordan is safe and welcoming for visitors; normal caution applies. Tap water in Amman is treated but not recommended for drinking, as rooftop storage tanks can harbour contamination, so drink bottled throughout. Petra involves long walks and uneven terrain in strong sun.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Very easy for vegetarians: the Levantine table is largely plant-based, with hummus, mutabbal, falafel and vegetable mezze everywhere. Jain travellers should flag onion and garlic, which are common. Indian food is limited outside Amman, so carry a few provisions for the Petra leg; Amman has a handful of Indian restaurants for a fix.
